proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(\kappa\ge0\).  Conditional on \(\lambda\), put \(z_t=\lambda+\epsilon_t\).  For every first-period comparison and every second-period comparison under every possible lag \(a\in M_1\), a tie is an affine hyperplane in \(\mathbb R^J\).  There are finitely many such hyperplanes.  Assumption \(\texttt{ass:absolute-continuity}\) therefore makes their conditional probability zero.  Off their union, the utility index in \(\texttt{ass:utility-index}\) and maximization in \(\texttt{ass:choice-maximization}\) determine one response table
\[
 f(z)=\bigl(f_1(z),(f_2(a;z):a\in M_1)\bigr).
\]
Every designated winner satisfies every strict comparison in \(\texttt{def:comparison-graph}\), so \(f(z)\in F_\kappa\) by \(\texttt{def:feasible-response-set}\).  Define, for almost every \(\lambda\),
\[
 q_f(\lambda)=\Pr\{f(\lambda+\epsilon_t)=f\mid\lambda\},
 \qquad f\in F_\kappa.
\]
Conditional homogeneity makes this definition independent of \(t\), and \(q(\lambda)\in\Delta(F_\kappa)\).

For \(a\in M_1\) and \(b\in M_2\), conditional independence of \(\epsilon_1\) and \(\epsilon_2\), together with the fact that the second-period rule uses the realized lag \(a\), gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \Pr(Y_1=a,Y_2=b\mid\lambda)
 &=\Pr\{f_1(z_1)=a\mid\lambda\}
   \Pr\{f_2(a;z_2)=b\mid\lambda\}\\
 &=r_a(q(\lambda))s_{ab}(q(\lambda))
 =v_{ab}(q(\lambda)).
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus the fixed-cell sequential-exogeneity and stationarity factorization used for necessity is exactly
\[
 P=\int v(q(\lambda))\,dF_\lambda(\lambda).
\]
The simplex \(\Delta(F_\kappa)\) is compact and \(v\) is continuous, so its image is compact.  Every image point lies in the affine hyperplane \(\sum_{a,b}x_{ab}=1\), of dimension \(m-1\).  If a convex representation uses more than \(m\) image points, the vectors obtained by adjoining a leading one are linearly dependent; perturbing the convex weights in that null direction until one becomes zero preserves the represented point.  Repetition leaves at most \(m\) image points.  Consequently the convex hull is the continuous image of a compact set of at most \(m\) points and their weights, hence is compact.  Finite simple-function approximations to the displayed integral belong to this convex hull and converge to \(P\); closedness therefore gives \(P\in\mathcal C_\kappa\).

Conversely, take \(P\in\mathcal C_\kappa\).  The same affine-dependence reduction gives
\[
 P=\sum_{\ell=1}^{L_0}\omega_\ell v(q^\ell),
 \qquad 1\le L_0\le m,
 \qquad \omega_\ell\ge0,
 \qquad \sum_{\ell=1}^{L_0}\omega_\ell=1.
\]
For every \(\ell\) and every \(f\) with \(q_f^\ell>0\), \(\texttt{lem:strict-cycle-feasibility}\) supplies an open axis-aligned cube \(B_{\ell f}\) contained in the strict response patch for \(f\).  Let \(G_\ell\) be the probability law assigning mass \(q_f^\ell\) uniformly on \(B_{\ell f}\).  This is an absolutely continuous law on \(\mathbb R^J\).  Choose distinct constants \(c_\ell\), set \(\lambda^\ell=(c_\ell,\ldots,c_\ell)\), and assign \(\Pr(\lambda=\lambda^\ell)=\omega_\ell\).  Conditional on \(\lambda=\lambda^\ell\), draw \(\epsilon_1\) and \(\epsilon_2\) independently from the translate of \(G_\ell\) by \(-\lambda^\ell\).  The two conditional shock laws are identical and absolutely continuous, while \(\lambda^\ell+\epsilon_t\sim G_\ell\).  Hence the conditional response-table law is exactly \(q^\ell\), the conditional path law is \(v(q^\ell)\), and mixing over \(\ell\) produces exactly \(P\).  Every draw lies in a strict patch, so choices are unique.  Zero weights and boundary path probabilities are obtained exactly, without a limiting argument.

The two directions use different class facts.  Necessity uses the fixed-cell conditional factorization supplied by conditional serial independence and conditional time homogeneity, with the no-tie regularity needed to obtain a response table almost surely.  Sufficiency is witnessed by the stronger conditionally iid, full-vector Lebesgue-absolutely-continuous construction just given.  Thus the equality proved here concerns the published fixed-cell model intersected with this explicit no-tie and absolute-continuity subclass, rather than every law in a broader published class.

There are finitely many deterministic response tables, and every comparison multigraph has finitely many directed simple cycles.  By \(\texttt{def:comparison-graph}\), each cycle weight is
\[
 W_C(\kappa)=A_C+B_C\kappa,
\]
where \(A_C\in\mathbb Q\) and \(B_C\in\mathbb Z\).  Each affine function with \(B_C\ne0\) has at most one root.  Hence adjoining zero to all nonnegative roots produces a finite rational set \(\mathcal B_{\mathrm{des}}\), and \(K=\max\mathcal B_{\mathrm{des}}\) is finite and rational.

Fix \(\kappa>K\).  If \(B_C>0\), then \(W_C(\kappa)>0\): when its root is nonnegative this follows from \(\kappa>K\), and when its root is negative it follows for every nonnegative \(\kappa\).  If \(B_C=0\), positivity is equivalent to \(A_C>0\).  If \(B_C<0\), the weight is negative to the right of a nonnegative root, or throughout the nonnegative half-line when its root is negative.  Therefore
\[
 W_C(\kappa)>0\text{ for every simple cycle }C
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \bigl[B_C>0\text{ or }(B_C=0\text{ and }A_C>0)\bigr]
 \text{ for every }C.
\]
By \(\texttt{lem:strict-cycle-feasibility}\) and \(\texttt{def:terminal-body}\), this is exactly
\[
 F_\kappa=F_\infty\qquad(\kappa>K).
\]
The quadratic map and convex-hull construction are then identical, so \(\texttt{thm:sharp-iid-body}\) yields
\[
 \mathcal C_\kappa=\mathcal C_\infty\qquad(\kappa>K).
\]

Assume \(\Theta(P)\ne\varnothing\), as required by \(\texttt{ass:correct-specification}\).  If \(P\in\mathcal C_\infty\), the preceding equality gives \((K,+\infty)\subseteq\Theta(P)\), hence \(U(P)=+\infty\).  If \(P\notin\mathcal C_\infty\), no \(\kappa>K\) belongs to \(\Theta(P)\); its nonempty identified set is bounded above by \(K\), so \(U(P)<+\infty\).  Compactness of \(\mathcal C_\infty\), supplied by the sharp-body theorem applied to \(F_\infty\), implies that its complement has strictly positive distance.  Therefore
\[
 U(P)<+\infty
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 P\notin\mathcal C_\infty
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 D_\infty(P)>0.
\]

Suppose \(P\in\mathcal C_{\kappa_0}\).  By the sharp-body theorem it has a finite representation using response laws \(q^\ell\).  Only finitely many response tables have positive weight.  Every simple-cycle weight for each such table is strictly positive at \(\kappa_0\); continuity of finitely many affine functions gives a relative neighborhood of \(\kappa_0\) in \([0,+\infty)\) on which all remain positive.  The same \(q^\ell\) and outer mixing weights therefore represent \(P\) throughout that neighborhood.  Hence \(\Theta(P)\) is relatively open.

Removing \(\mathcal B_{\mathrm{des}}\) partitions \([0,+\infty)\) into finitely many open strata.  On each stratum no cycle weight changes sign, so \(F_\kappa\), \(\mathcal C_\kappa\), and the membership decision for \(P\) are constant.  Relative openness rules out isolated compatible breakpoints.  It follows that \(\Theta(P)\) is a finite union of relatively open intervals.  Every finite upper endpoint is a stratum boundary in \(\mathcal B_{\mathrm{des}}\), and relative openness shows that it is not attained.

For a fixed enumerated response set \(F\), membership has the explicit finite semialgebraic certificate
\[
\begin{gathered}
 w_\ell\ge0,\qquad \sum_{\ell=1}^{m}w_\ell=1,
 \qquad q_{\ell f}\ge0,\qquad \sum_{f\in F}q_{\ell f}=1,\\
 P_{ab}=\sum_{\ell=1}^{m}w_\ell
 \left(\sum_{f\in F}q_{\ell f}\mathbf 1\{f_1=a\}\right)
 \left(\sum_{f\in F}q_{\ell f}\mathbf 1\{f_2(a)=b\}\right)
 \quad(a\in M_1,b\in M_2).
\end{gathered}
\]
All coefficients are rational, all variables and constraints are displayed, and the bound of \(m\) outer components was proved above.  A finite exact sign-decomposition procedure applies: project successively using the finitely many coefficients, discriminants, and pairwise resultants in the last variable; isolate the resulting univariate real roots by signed polynomial-remainder sequences and rational isolating intervals; and lift one sign-invariant cell at a time.  The number of variables falls at every projection step, while every lift has finitely many algebraic boundary roots, so the recursion terminates and returns either an algebraic feasible point or the finite list of sign-invariant cells certifying infeasibility.  Testing one representative of each open price stratum and each breakpoint value with this certified procedure therefore recovers every interval of \(\Theta(P)\); the largest compatible stratum boundary is the exact finite value of \(U(P)\).  This search does not presume nesting or monotonicity in \(\kappa\).

Finally, let \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{ac}}\) denote the maintained absolutely continuous fixed-cell subclass and let \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{pub}}\) be any broader published fixed-cell class containing it.  When \(P\in\mathcal C_\infty\), the sharp-body construction supplies, for every \(\kappa>K\), a rationalizing law inside \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{ac}}\); the conclusion \(U(P)=+\infty\) therefore transfers upward to \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{pub}}\) by subclass inclusion.  In contrast, \(P\notin\mathcal C_\infty\) excludes only laws covered by the necessity argument for \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{ac}}\).  Nonmembership in a subclass-generated body is not, by set inclusion alone, an exclusion certificate for a larger class, so the finite-ceiling direction does not transfer upward without separately proving necessity for that larger class.

Fix \(H\in\{F_\kappa,F_\infty\}\) and write \(N=|H|\).  First, \(H\) is nonempty.  For finite \(\kappa\), choose \(z\) outside the finite collection of tie hyperplanes and let its strict maximizers in all required contexts define \(f\); then all constraints of \(G_{\kappa,f}\) hold, so \(f\in F_\kappa\).  For the terminal set, choose an unbounded sequence \(\kappa_j\) and such an induced table at every \(\kappa_j\).  Since there are finitely many tables, one table \(f\) occurs along an unbounded subsequence.  Every affine cycle weight \(A_C+B_C\kappa_j\) for that table is positive on this subsequence.  Hence \(B_C>0\), or \(B_C=0\) and \(A_C>0\); \(B_C<0\) is impossible.  Thus \(f\in F_\infty\).

Take \(q\in\Delta(H)\).  By \(\texttt{lem:observable-moment-compression}\), there is \(\bar q\in\Delta(H)\) with
\[
 v(\bar q)=v(q),
 \qquad h:=|\operatorname{supp}(\bar q)|\le\min\{N,m\}.
\]
If \(h=1\), then \(\bar q\in\mathcal G_{H,L}\) for every \(L\), so set \(q'=\bar q\).  If \(h\ge2\), order its support as \(f_1,\ldots,f_h\) and define
\[
 q'_{f_j}=\frac{\lfloor L\bar q_{f_j}\rfloor}{L}\quad(j<h),
 \qquad
 q'_{f_h}=1-\sum_{j<h}q'_{f_j},
\]
with all other coordinates zero.  Then \(q'\in\mathcal G_{H,L}\), and
\[
 \|\bar q-q'\|_1
 =2\sum_{j<h}\left(\bar q_{f_j}-q'_{f_j}\right)
 \le\frac{2(h-1)}{L}
 \le\frac{2(\min\{N,m\}-1)}{L}.
\]
For any two probability vectors \(x,x'\) on \(H\) and any subset \(E\subseteq H\), cancellation of the total signed mass gives
\[
 |x(E)-x'(E)|\le\frac12\|x-x'\|_1.
\]
Both \(r_a\) and \(s_{ab}\) are probabilities of subsets of \(H\).  With \(\Delta=\|\bar q-q'\|_1\), therefore,
\[
 |r_a(\bar q)-r_a(q')|\le\frac\Delta2,
 \qquad
 |s_{ab}(\bar q)-s_{ab}(q')|\le\frac\Delta2.
\]
Because all factors lie in \([0,1]\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 |v_{ab}(q)-v_{ab}(q')|
 &=|v_{ab}(\bar q)-v_{ab}(q')|\\
 &\le |r_a(\bar q)-r_a(q')|s_{ab}(\bar q)
      +r_a(q')|s_{ab}(\bar q)-s_{ab}(q')|\\
 &\le\Delta.
\end{aligned}
\]
The left side is also at most one.  With the corrected construction
\[
 e_{H,L}=\min\left\{1,\frac{2(\min\{N,m\}-1)}{L}\right\},
\]
we have proved \(\|v(q)-v(q')\|_\infty\le e_{H,L}\).

The grid image is contained in the full image, so \(\mathcal C_{H,L}\subseteq\mathcal C_H\).  Conversely, for
\[
 Q=\sum_{j=1}^s\theta_jv(q^j)\in\mathcal C_H,
 \qquad \theta_j\ge0,
 \qquad \sum_j\theta_j=1,
\]
apply the preceding compression and rounding separately to each \(q^j\), producing \(q^{j\prime}\in\mathcal G_{H,L}\).  Then
\[
 Q_L=\sum_j\theta_jv(q^{j\prime})\in\mathcal C_{H,L},
 \qquad
 \|Q-Q_L\|_\infty
 \le\sum_j\theta_j\|v(q^j)-v(q^{j\prime})\|_\infty
 \le e_{H,L}.
\]
This proves
\[
 \mathcal C_{H,L}\subseteq\mathcal C_H
 \subseteq\mathcal C_{H,L}+[-e_{H,L},e_{H,L}]^m.
\]

Both bodies are compact.  The first inclusion gives
\[
 \operatorname{dist}_\infty(R,\mathcal C_H)\le d_{H,L}(R).
\]
For a nearest \(Q\in\mathcal C_H\), take the preceding \(Q_L\).  The triangle inequality yields
\[
 d_{H,L}(R)
 \le\|R-Q_L\|_\infty
 \le\operatorname{dist}_\infty(R,\mathcal C_H)+e_{H,L}.
\]
Rearranging and using nonnegativity proves the two-sided distance bound.

For rational certification, enumerate the finite grid image as rational vectors \(x^1,\ldots,x^G\).  For rational \(R\), \(d_{H,L}(R)\) is the value of the rational linear program
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
 \text{minimize}&\delta\\
 \text{over}&\delta\ge0,\ \omega_g\ge0\\
 \text{subject to}&\displaystyle\sum_{g=1}^G\omega_g=1,\\
 &\displaystyle-\delta\le R_j-\sum_{g=1}^G\omega_gx^g_j\le\delta,
 \quad j=1,\ldots,m.
\end{array}
\]
The corresponding lower-certificate system is
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
 \text{maximize}&u^\top R-t\\
 \text{over}&u=u^+-u^-,\quad u^+,u^-\ge0,\quad t\in\mathbb R\\
 \text{subject to}&\displaystyle\sum_{j=1}^m(u_j^++u_j^-)\le1,\\
 &t\ge u^\top x^g,\quad g=1,\ldots,G.
\end{array}
\]
Indeed, for every primal mixture \(x=\sum_g\omega_gx^g\) and every displayed lower certificate,
\[
 u^\top R-t\le u^\top(R-x)\le\|R-x\|_\infty,
\]
which is weak duality.  If the minimum is zero, \(u=0\) and \(t=0\) give equality.  If it is positive, then at a minimizing point \(x^*\), the active signed coordinates of \(R-x^*\) generate a supporting functional \(u\) of \(\ell_1\)-norm one for the minimizing face; otherwise a convex combination of grid points would give a feasible direction that strictly decreases every active signed residual, contradicting minimality.  For this \(u\), set \(t=\max_gu^\top x^g=u^\top x^*\).  Then
\[
 u^\top R-t=u^\top(R-x^*)=\|R-x^*\|_\infty=d_{H,L}(R),
\]
so the two certificate systems have the same value.  All constraints are rational.  Enumerating their finitely many active sets and solving each full-rank subsystem by rational Gaussian elimination yields rational optimal basic feasible certificates; direct substitution checks every inequality and equality.  Stopping earlier with feasible upper and lower certificates whose objective values differ by at most any prescribed positive rational tolerance gives rational \(d^-\le d_{H,L}(R)\le d^+\).

With \(L_n=n\), \(\eta_n=1/n\), and \(R=\widehat P\), rationality follows from the multinomial counts.  The certified inequalities and the deterministic sandwich give
\[
 \underline D_{H,n}
 =\max\{0,d^-_{H,n}-e_{H,L_n}\}
 \le\operatorname{dist}_\infty(\widehat P,\mathcal C_H).
\]
Finally \(e_{H,L}\to0\) for fixed finite \(H\), now at the observable-compressed rate \(2(\min\{|H|,m\}-1)/L\), and the primal--dual gap can be made arbitrarily small.  Choosing both errors below half of any requested positive tolerance proves finite refinement to that distance precision.

For each path cell \(j=(a,b)\), put \(X_{ij}=\mathbf 1\{Y_{i1}=a,Y_{i2}=b\}\).  By \(\texttt{ass:iid-consumers}\), these variables are iid Bernoulli with mean \(P_j\).  If \(X\) is Bernoulli with mean \(p\), differentiating
\[
 \log\mathbb E\exp\{s(X-p)\}=-sp+\log(1-p+pe^s)
\]
twice and bounding the resulting Bernoulli variance by \(1/4\), with value and first derivative zero at \(s=0\), gives
\[
 \log\mathbb E e^{s(X-p)}\le\frac{s^2}{8}.
\]
Markov's inequality applied to \(\exp\{s\sum_i(X_{ij}-P_j)\}\), followed by minimization at \(s=4x\), gives
\[
 \Pr\{\widehat P_j-P_j\ge x\}\le e^{-2nx^2}.
\]
Applying the same argument to \(-s\) gives the lower tail.  The union bound over all \(m\) cells and the definition
\[
 \rho_{n,\alpha}=\sqrt{\frac{\log(2m/\alpha)}{2n}}
\]
therefore imply
\[
 \Pr(E_n)\ge1-\alpha,
 \qquad
 E_n:=\{\|\widehat P-P\|_\infty\le\rho_{n,\alpha}\}.
\]
This bound contains no unknown feature of the data-generating law, so it is uniform over the maintained class.

Fix \(\kappa\in\Theta(P)\), and let \(H\) be the response set assigned to its open stratum or breakpoint.  Then \(P\in\mathcal C_H\).  On \(E_n\),
\[
 \operatorname{dist}_\infty(\widehat P,\mathcal C_H)
 \le\|\widehat P-P\|_\infty
 \le\rho_{n,\alpha}.
\]
The improved certified-approximation theorem gives, with
\[
 e_{H,L_n}=\min\left\{1,\frac{2(\min\{|H|,m\}-1)}{n}\right\},
\]
the correctly typed inequality
\[
 \underline D_{H,n}
 \le\operatorname{dist}_\infty(\widehat P,\mathcal C_H)
 \le\rho_{n,\alpha}.
\]
Thus the confidence-set rule retains the entire open stratum or the breakpoint containing \(\kappa\).  If \(\kappa>K\), the terminal-frontier theorem gives \(H=F_\infty\), and the same argument applies to the separate terminal test.  Hence
\[
 E_n\subseteq\{\Theta(P)\subseteq\widehat\Theta_{n,\alpha}\},
\]
and the preceding probability bound proves simultaneous whole-set coverage.  There is no multiplicity penalty over \(\kappa\), because all retention conclusions hold on the same event \(E_n\).  By construction, retention of the terminal stratum includes all of \((K,+\infty)\), so the reported upper endpoint is \(+\infty\).

For consistency, suppose \(\delta=D_\infty(P)>0\).  The certified optimization gap implies
\[
 d^-_{F_\infty,n}
 \ge d_{\infty,L_n}(\widehat P)-\eta_n.
\]
Since \(\mathcal C_{\infty,L_n}\subseteq\mathcal C_\infty\), the reverse triangle inequality gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \underline D_{F_\infty,n}
 &\ge d_{\infty,L_n}(\widehat P)-\eta_n-e_{F_\infty,L_n}\\
 &\ge\operatorname{dist}_\infty(\widehat P,\mathcal C_\infty)
      -\eta_n-e_{F_\infty,L_n}\\
 &\ge\delta-\|\widehat P-P\|_\infty
      -\eta_n-e_{F_\infty,L_n}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The first inequality also holds when its right side is negative, because \(\underline D_{F_\infty,n}\ge0\).  Here
\[
 \eta_n=\frac1n\longrightarrow0,
 \qquad
 e_{F_\infty,L_n}
 \le\frac{2(\min\{|F_\infty|,m\}-1)}{n}\longrightarrow0,
 \qquad
 \rho_{n,\alpha}\longrightarrow0.
\]
The same exponential bound implies \(\|\widehat P-P\|_\infty\to0\) in probability.  Therefore
\[
 \Pr\{\underline D_{F_\infty,n}>\rho_{n,\alpha}\}\longrightarrow1.
\]
With probability tending to one the terminal stratum is rejected, and every remaining retained piece lies in \([0,K]\); the reported upper endpoint is therefore finite.  No uniform-consistency assertion is made when \(D_\infty(P)=0\).

added_lemmas.statement:
For every nonempty finite \(H\in\{F_\kappa,F_\infty\}\), define
\[
 T_H(q)=\bigl((r_a(q))_{a\in M_1},(s_{ab}(q))_{a\in M_1,b\in M_2}\bigr).
\]
If \(d_H=\operatorname{affdim}\operatorname{conv}T_H(\Delta(H))\), then
\[
 d_H\le m-1.
\]
For every \(q\in\Delta(H)\), there is \(\bar q\in\Delta(H)\) such that
\[
 T_H(\bar q)=T_H(q),\qquad v(\bar q)=v(q),
 \qquad |\operatorname{supp}(\bar q)|\le d_H+1\le\min\{|H|,m\}.
\]
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Put \(k=|M_1|\).  The map \(T_H\) is linear in \(q\).  For every \(q\in\Delta(H)\), its coordinates obey
\[
 \sum_{a\in M_1}r_a(q)=1,
 \qquad
 \sum_{b\in M_2}s_{ab}(q)=1\quad(a\in M_1).
\]
These are \(k+1\) linearly independent affine equations on the \(k+m\) coordinates of \(T_H(q)\): the first uses only the \(r\)-block, and each of the remaining equations uses a distinct row of the \(s\)-block.  Hence
\[
 d_H\le (k+m)-(k+1)=m-1.
\]
Also, the affine dimension of the convex hull of the \(|H|\) vectors \(T_H(e_f)\), \(f\in H\), is at most \(|H|-1\), so \(d_H+1\le\min\{|H|,m\}\).

It remains to prove the support assertion without invoking an additional hypothesis.  Since \(T_H\) is linear,
\[
 T_H(q)=\sum_{f\in H}q_fT_H(e_f).
\]
If more than \(d_H+1\) coefficients on the right are positive, the corresponding vectors \((1,T_H(e_f))\) are linearly dependent.  Thus there are real numbers \(c_f\), not all zero and vanishing off the current support, such that
\[
 
 \sum_fc_f=0,
 \qquad
 \sum_fc_fT_H(e_f)=0.
\]
After replacing \(c\) by \(-c\) if necessary, some \(c_f>0\).  Set
\[
 t=\min_{f:c_f>0}\frac{q_f}{c_f}>0,
 \qquad q'_f=q_f-tc_f.
\]
For \(c_f>0\), the definition of \(t\) gives \(q'_f\ge0\); for \(c_f\le0\), one has \(q'_f\ge q_f\ge0\).  Moreover,
\[
 \sum_fq'_f=1,
 \qquad T_H(q')=T_H(q),
\]
and at least one positive coefficient becomes zero.  Repeating this finite reduction produces \(\bar q\) with support at most \(d_H+1\).  Finally, the defining identity \(v_{ab}(q)=r_a(q)s_{ab}(q)\) shows coordinate by coordinate that equality of \(T_H\)-moments implies \(v(\bar q)=v(q)\).

proposed.name: Observable-compressed rational-grid inner body and outer inflation
proposed.construction:
For each \(H\in\{F_\kappa,F_\infty\}\), form \(\mathcal G_{H,L}=\{q\in\Delta(H):Lq_f\in\mathbb Z\text{ for every }f\in H\}\), set \(\mathcal C_{H,L}=\operatorname{conv}v(\mathcal G_{H,L})\), and inflate this inner body by \([-e_{H,L},e_{H,L}]^m\), where
\[
 e_{H,L}=\min\left\{1,\frac{2(\min\{|H|,m\}-1)}{L}\right\}.
\]
The notation is evaluated separately with \(H=F_\kappa\) and \(H=F_\infty\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: The grid construction must use the equal-moment support bound of at most \(\min\{|H|,m\}\) response tables.

proposed.name: Certified whole-identified-set confidence region with observable-compressed error
proposed.construction:
Set \(L_n=n\) and \(\eta_n=1/n\).  Compute the simultaneous box \(\|\widehat P-P\|_\infty\le\rho_{n,\alpha}\).  For every finite open price stratum and every breakpoint value, use its own \(F_\kappa\) to compute rational primal and dual bounds \(d^-_{F_\kappa,n}\le d_{\kappa,L_n}(\widehat P)\le d^+_{F_\kappa,n}\) with gap at most \(\eta_n\), set
\[
 \underline D_{F_\kappa,n}
 =\max\{0,d^-_{F_\kappa,n}-e_{F_\kappa,L_n}\},
 \qquad
 e_{F_\kappa,L_n}
 =\min\left\{1,\frac{2(\min\{|F_\kappa|,m\}-1)}{L_n}\right\},
\]
and retain that parameter piece if and only if \(\underline D_{F_\kappa,n}\le\rho_{n,\alpha}\).  Separately use \(F_\infty\) to compute \(d^-_{F_\infty,n}\), set
\[
 \underline D_{F_\infty,n}
 =\max\{0,d^-_{F_\infty,n}-e_{F_\infty,L_n}\},
 \qquad
 e_{F_\infty,L_n}
 =\min\left\{1,\frac{2(\min\{|F_\infty|,m\}-1)}{L_n}\right\},
\]
and retain the terminal stratum \((K,+\infty)\) if and only if \(\underline D_{F_\infty,n}\le\rho_{n,\alpha}\).  The union is \(\widehat\Theta_{n,\alpha}\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: Every finite-stratum and terminal test must propagate the corrected grid error, and the malformed lower-distance inequality is written with a genuine \(\le\) relation.

proposed.statement: For every finite \(J\), every \(L\ge1\), and each \(H\in\{F_\kappa,F_\infty\}\), \(\mathcal C_{H,L}\subseteq\mathcal C_H\subseteq\mathcal C_{H,L}+[-e_{H,L},e_{H,L}]^m\). Consequently, for every probability table \(R\), \(\max\{0,d_{H,L}(R)-e_{H,L}\}\le\operatorname{dist}_\infty(R,\mathcal C_H)\le d_{H,L}(R)\). For rational \(R\), the finite convex-hull program admits rational primal and dual certificates \(d^-\le d_{H,L}(R)\le d^+\) with any prescribed positive rational gap; in particular, \(L_n=n\) and \(\eta_n=1/n\) yield \(d^+-d^-\le\eta_n\) and \(\underline D_{H,n}=\max\{0,d^-_{H,n}-e_{H,L_n}\}\le\operatorname{dist}_\infty(\widehat P,\mathcal C_H)\). Refinement reaches any requested strictly positive distance precision.
proposed.justification: Observable-moment compression makes the deterministic sandwich scale with at most the observed path dimension rather than the potentially exponential number of response tables.
proposed.gap: Duarte et al. give progressively refined valid bounds for a general polynomial program, but not this conditional-iid quadratic-body compression, its closed deterministic error, or separate finite-stratum and terminal certificates.
proposed.consumer: Cells with more than three plans receive auditable included-point certificates, excluded-point separators, and a stopping rule whose deterministic error depends on \(\min\{|H|,m\}\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: The theorem now declares the observable-moment compression lemma and the finite response-set constructions used to justify nonemptiness as its complete proof spine.

open_obligations.what_is_open: The complete latent-free projection remains open for negative entry with both off-diagonal probabilities positive, zero-sign entry, and all six exit bodies, including every equality and zero-probability boundary and an explicit attaining mixture in each regime.
open_obligations.obstruction: The exact negative-entry cone has eight coupled quadratic curve families sharing four square-coordinate budgets.  When both off-diagonal coordinates are positive, its dual support function contains a switching term involving the smaller off-diagonal mass.  Separate face optimization is therefore only an outer description, and a generic unevaluated quantifier-elimination call is excluded by the target.
open_obligations.attempted: Strict-cycle enumeration was completed for all nine terminal classes.  All twenty two-patch curves were checked, pure rays were removed, negative and zero-sign entry were reduced to eight and seven nonredundant curve families, the two off-diagonal dual coefficients were eliminated, and positive-sign entry plus two negative-sign boundary faces were solved constructively.  The unresolved route is the joint positive-off-diagonal active-allocation split, followed by the analogous three-first-choice allocation for exit.
open_obligations.partial_result:
Relabel the continuing plans \(a,b\), write
\[
 (A,B,C,R,S,T)=(P_{aa},P_{ab},P_{ac},P_{ba},P_{bb},P_{bc}),
\]
and put \(\tau=(p_{1a}-p_{1b})-(p_{2a}-p_{2b})\).  Strict-cycle enumeration gives the terminal entry response tables
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
&f_1=a&f_1=b\\ \hline
\tau<0&aaa,aab,aac,acc&bab,bac,bbb,bcb,bcc\\
\tau=0&aaa,aac,acc&bab,bac,bbb,bcb,bcc\\
\tau>0&aaa,aac,acc&baa,bab,bac,bbb,bcb,bcc.
\end{array}
\]
For exit, write \(L_0=bbb\), \(L_1=abb\), \(L_2=aba\), and \(L_3=aaa\).  The permitted indices for first choices \(a,b,c\), in that order, are
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c|c|c}
\text{initial status}&\operatorname{sign}(\tau)&a&b&c\\ \hline
b\text{ continues}&-&\{2,3\}&\{0,1,2\}&\{0,1,2,3\}\\
b\text{ continues}&0&\{3\}&\{0,1,2\}&\{0,1,2,3\}\\
b\text{ continues}&+&\{3\}&\{0,1,2,3\}&\{0,1,2,3\}\\
c\text{ exits}&-&\{1,2,3\}&\{0,1\}&\{0,1,2,3\}\\
c\text{ exits}&0&\{2,3\}&\{0,1\}&\{0,1,2,3\}\\
c\text{ exits}&+&\{2,3\}&\{0,1,2\}&\{0,1,2,3\}.
\end{array}
\]
Each listed patch is open and nonempty.

For nonnegative \(a,c,s,h,b\), define
\[
 \Phi(a,c,s,h;b)=
 \bigl[bc\le h(a+c)\ \wedge\ b^2\le s(a+c)\bigr]
 \vee
 \bigl[bc>h(a+c)\ \wedge\ c(b-h)^2+ah^2\le sac\bigr].
\]
The complete positive-sign entry result is
\[
 P\in\mathcal C_\infty
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 B\le R+T\ \wedge\ \Phi(A,C,S,T;B)
 \qquad(\tau>0).
\]
It includes all zero boundaries.  Two complete negative-sign faces are
\[
\begin{aligned}
 R=0:\quad&P\in\mathcal C_\infty
 \Longleftrightarrow S\ge L\ \wedge\ \Phi(A,C,S-L,H;B),
 &L&=\max\{0,B-T\},\quad H=\min\{B,T\};\\
 B=0:\quad&P\in\mathcal C_\infty
 \Longleftrightarrow A\ge L\ \wedge\ R^2\le(A-L)(S+T),
 &L&=\max\{0,R-C\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The maxima and minima expand into polynomial branches, and the corresponding proofs allocate rank-one masses explicitly.

The full negative-entry cone is exactly generated by the four pure rays in coordinates \(A,C,S,T\) and, for \(s,t\ge0\), the eight curves
\[
\begin{array}{l}
(s^2+st,0,0,st,t^2,0),\\
(s^2+st,0,0,st,0,t^2),\\
(s^2,st,0,st,t^2,0),\\
(s^2,0,st,st,t^2,0),\\
(s^2,0,st,st,0,t^2),\\
(s^2,st,0,0,t^2+st,0),\\
(s^2,st,0,0,t^2,st),\\
(0,st,s^2,0,t^2,st).
\end{array}
\]
The zero-sign cone removes the sixth curve.  If \(a,c,s,t\ge0\) are dual coefficients on the pure-ray coordinates and \(b,r\) are the coefficients on \(B,R\), nonnegativity on these curves is equivalent to
\[
 r\ge-\rho,\qquad b\ge-\beta,\qquad b+r\ge-\gamma,
\]
where
\[
 \rho=\min(a,c)+2\sqrt{a\min(s,t)},
 \quad
 \beta=\min\{s+2\sqrt{as},t+2\sqrt{as},t+2\sqrt{cs}\},
 \quad
 \gamma=2\sqrt{as}.
\]
For fixed \(a,c,s,t\), minimizing over \(b,r\) gives
\[
 -\left[B\beta+R\rho-\min(B,R)\max\{\beta+\rho-\gamma,0\}\right].
\]
The coupled final term is the exact obstruction to intersecting the two solved faces when \(B,R>0\).

prose_updates.tldr: Within one known fixed design cell, the project represents conditional-iid turnover probabilities as the convex hull of a quadratic response-table map.  Strict comparison graphs yield finitely many rational price breakpoints, after which the compatible body is constant; separation from that terminal body is exactly the finite switching-cost-ceiling criterion for the maintained absolutely continuous subclass.  Exact finite semialgebraic feasibility recovers the frontier, and observable-moment compression gives certified finite-menu approximation and simultaneous multinomial inversion.  The constructive three-plan analysis currently covers positive-sign entry and two negative-sign boundary faces; the complete latent-free Boolean elimination for the remaining entry and exit classes remains \(\texttt{oeq:three-plan-analytic-body}\), not a claimed result.

project_justification.fill: The project derives the finite terminal comparison graph, represents each exact compatible body as the convex hull of a conditional-iid quadratic map, proves the observable finite-ceiling frontier, and recovers the exact identified set through finitely many rational price strata with certified semialgebraic feasibility.  It supplies constructive three-plan formulas for positive-sign entry and two informative negative-sign boundary faces while leaving the complete latent-free Boolean elimination as \(\texttt{oeq:three-plan-analytic-body}\).  For arbitrary finite menus, equal-moment compression and rational-grid linear programs provide a deterministic error bound and a uniformly covering inference layer.

prose_updates.honest_scope: The result concerns one known two-choice design cell with stable plan quality, a common \(\kappa\), unrestricted fixed-effect mixing, conditional serial independence and time homogeneity, and conditionally iid shocks whose full-vector conditional laws are Lebesgue absolutely continuous.  Necessity uses the resulting fixed-cell sequential-exogeneity and stationarity factorization; constructive sufficiency uses the stronger open-patch absolute-continuity regularity.  Accordingly, the exact body is for the published fixed-cell class intersected with explicit no-tie and absolute-continuity conditions, not the whole broader published class.  A terminal rationalization constructed inside this subclass also proves nonidentification in any containing class, but failure to belong to the subclass terminal body does not by inclusion alone exclude rationalization in the larger class.  The note does not identify welfare, validate changing plan quality, impose monotonicity of \(\Theta(P)\), promise polynomial-time computation, claim a complete three-plan elimination, or claim uniform consistency when \(D_\infty(P)=0\).

statement_notes.justification: Necessity converts fixed-cell sequential exogeneity and time homogeneity into a mixture of product response probabilities; sufficiency constructs conditionally iid full-vector absolutely continuous shocks inside strict patches.  The exact equality is therefore asserted for the maintained no-tie subclass.

The theorem gives the exact observable finite-ceiling criterion for the maintained subclass.  Its terminal rationalization and hence the infinite-ceiling direction transfer to any containing class, whereas terminal exclusion does not transfer upward by subclass inclusion alone.

The moment vector has affine dimension at most \(m-1\), so every quadratic image point has an equal-moment representative on at most \(\min\{|H|,m\}\) tables and the grid error avoids exponential response-table dependence.
